question: Nursery children who loved drawing got a certificate for it. Which group later drew less in free time?
answer: Those promised it in advance. In Lepper, Greene and Nisbett's study, children who drew to earn an expected award later chose drawing less than before; children given the same award as a surprise did not. A reward announced beforehand turns play into a job. Pooled studies by Deci and colleagues found the same pattern.
move: A reward announced in advance changes why a person does the task.
ask: When I offer someone a reward, am I adding to their reasons or replacing them?
trap: Thinking any reward, expected or not, spoils the pleasure.
reference: Lepper, Greene & Nisbett, Undermining children's intrinsic interest with extrinsic reward: a test of the overjustification hypothesis, Journal of Personality and Social Psychology, 1973
